summary: All active uses retain I.1 creation. Human/child, hair and universe objects differ in participant type, not verbal meaning.
L-marked divine agent can precede or follow the verb; created objects are zero-marked or indexed by feminine -o- (74/4,115/189). Beneficiary l-NPs are distinct from agents in84/14,45.
PrS55/2 contrasts planned first-person plural creation in a purpose clause with realized third-person singular creation by Christ.

The inherited Detransitive Preterit xliq aʕma zʕuro has the boy as patient subject and a mother-associated ʕam phrase. The narrative places it with pregnancy; the edition's got-a-boy rendering does not alone distinguish conception from birth.
Existing unlabelled examples are counted under implicit sense1. Detransitive1 is inherited through its examples although no separate gloss list is printed.

Second round, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. English quotations are the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; semantic decisions are based on the Turoyo. Earlier-round proposals are inherited for context only and are not repeated in this JSON.
Active Preterit already reaches five after round 1. L-marked li dawle with xləqla Jan 3.6/74 confirms agent coding previously attested with divine agent, without a new sense.
Finite məxləq/məxləqiwo fills new Detransitive Infectum and Infectum-wa boxes; the inherited implicit Detransitive sense 1 is retained without inventing a second birth/creation sense.

xaloqo occurs already in inherited xlq.I.t.preterit.2. Jan applies the agent noun to a human troublemaker; this does not prove a new verbal Part act. paradigm. The create + abstract noun combinations remain lexical create, not established light-verb idioms.

Agentless creatures arising from soil and institutional/discussion creation extend the inherited Detransitive event beyond a child; no new sense number is assigned.
